item.content:encoded: I'm actually only vaguely familiar with Kurt Angle since I barely watch wrestling these days. I was mainly thinking of the evil foreigner routine Boris Zhukov did in the '80s, where he'd come out waving the hammer-and-sickle flag and want the audience to stand while he sang the Soviet national anthem. Since Blackwood is an English nationalist, and he's booked against the all-American hero, it made sense to have him play a jerk who thinks the colonists need some adult supervision.

item.content:encoded: This was during Undertaker's Deadman period, so I didn't think I could reasonably book him against Able by the logic of that era. You might be able to do Able as a face if it were the Attitude era and he was a Steve Austin-ish anti-hero, but this is 1991 - the year that Robocop saved Sting from a beating at the hands of the Four Horsemen, Hulk Hogan single-handedly won the Gulf War by bodyslamming Sgt. Slaughter, and a man in a chicken suit jumped out of a giant egg and then spent five minutes dancing with Mean Gene to "Turkey In the Straw".

This takes me back to the time in college when I actually watched pro wrestling. I enjoyed it more once I realized it was a soap opera based on ridiculous levels of machismo. Unrelated, this was also the same time that I watched the single season of DragonBall Z I ever saw, which I now realize I enjoyed for similar reasons. All the ridiculousness is there, even if I don't recognize half of the wrestlers.

ALL THOSE WHO FACE ME SHALL FALL LIKE DOMINOS ON A CHESS BOARD BEFORE THE MIGHT OF MY MONOPOLY!

This is brilliant. And also in character.

This is the best thing since the Able/682 rap battle. I am not even kidding.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The Ultimate Warrior, alias Jim Hellwig, was one of the worst wrestlers of all time. Not because he didn't know how to wrestle (he wasn't that good) or because he didn't know how to work a crowd (he did), but because he didn't appreciate anything that he was given as a performer.

Excellent wrestlers like Rick Rude or Randy Savage were the ones working their asses off to make him look half-way decent. This totally should have been Able versus The Undertakers. Two people who die and just keep getting back up again. The Urn versus SCP-072? That would have been friggin' excellent.

As it is.. It's not bad, and I could have really done without the Blackwood reference, but…

Jesus. This thing made me just grin the entire time. I think you really had to grow up with a lot of this to appreciate it at all.

So… Sure. +1.

Don't make me regret this.

This is something that's been kicking around in my head for a few weeks. I decided to write it as a little breather from all the contest stuff.

I regret nothing.
